name: list-detail
title: List / detail
description: Master/detail: a list of items beside the selected item's detail. Collapses to stacked navigation (list screen → detail screen) on narrow viewports and native phones.

frame.summary: Header, optional rail, then a list pane (dense rows — CLAUDE.md's list/table case) and a detail pane. Detail may host a Panel for metadata.

regions.name: list-pane
regions.purpose: Search/filter toolbar and the item list.
regions.collapse: Narrow: the list is the whole screen at /items.

regions.name: detail-pane
regions.collapse: Narrow: replaces the list; a back link returns to it.

regions.name: inspector
regions.collapse: Becomes a Sheet (the playground's Panel → Sheet swap at NARROW).

components.name: search
components.for: Filter the list; landmark false if TopNav has global search.

components.name: list
components.for: Selectable item rows with aria-current on the open one.

components.name: breadcrumbs
components.for: Back to the list on narrow.

dependsOnFuture.for: The item list — the template's core.

dependsOnFuture.interim: Row actions in the detail pane only.

behavior.summary: Selection is a URL (/items/:id). Wide: both panes, list keeps its scroll position. Narrow: one pane at a time, driven by the same URL — the list at /items, the detail at /items/:id.

decisions.decision: Selection is navigation, so rows are links with aria-current="page"
decisions.why: Not a listbox: opening an item changes the URL, works with middle-click and back, and is the same behaviour SideNav rows have. A listbox would need arrow-key roving focus and gives none of that.

decisions.decision: One URL scheme for both layouts
decisions.why: Narrow and wide differ only in which panes render, so resizing or rotating never loses the reader's place, and native deep links map 1:1.

decisions.decision: Focus moves to the detail heading on open in narrow mode only
decisions.why: On narrow the list disappears, so focus must go somewhere; on wide the reader may be scanning the list with arrow/tab and should stay there.

decisions.decision: Detail heading is h1 when narrow, h2 when wide
decisions.why: Open question rather than settled: wide has the list pane's h1 (area name); narrow detail is its own screen. Alternative: always h1 = area name visually hidden on narrow, detail h2.

decisions.decision: Empty detail on wide shows an empty-state, not the first item
decisions.why: Auto-selecting moves the URL without the reader asking and marks something read.

landmarks.label: implicit; target of the skip link

headingOutline.content: Selected item title — detail pane (h1 on narrow detail screen; see decision)

obligations: First focusable element is a skip link to <main> — there is no skip-link component, so it is VisuallyHidden content that becomes visible on :focus-visible (open question: promote to a component).
The list announces result count changes politely after search.

steps.change: Stacked navigation: list screen ↔ detail screen; inspector as Sheet.

responsive.notes: Uses all three breakpoint classes adopted by decision B2 (narrow / medium / wide) — the only spec that needs medium.

native.reason: App template: gets a native version by decision B3. Native is pro tier (decision N6) while the web version stays free; the registry field for that is proposed in docs/platforms.md §3.
native.mapping: Phone: navigation stack — list root, detail pushed, swipe-back. Tablet/foldable: two-column split view with the same selection model.
native.ios: NavigationSplitView (collapses to a stack on compact width automatically).
native.android: ListDetailPaneScaffold (Material 3 adaptive), single pane on compact.

tokenGaps.need: Narrow / medium / wide breakpoint tokens — adopted by decision B2, names and values pending the design-tokens interview
tokenGaps.interim: The block is intrinsic (auto-fill grid, flex-wrap) and needs none. Where a step is unavoidable the page owns the query, as the playground owns its single 60rem NARROW query in use-media-query.ts, until the B2 tokens land.

tokenGaps.need: A pane-width scale for split layouts
tokenGaps.interim: Derived from size.control.lg multiples (9, 10), matching the system's existing habit; three multipliers in three places is the point at which a token is justified.
Composed from visually-hidden; every template needs one, which is the argument for making it a component.

tokenGaps.need: A z-index / layer scale for the sticky header
tokenGaps.interim: The playground uses z-index: 1 with a comment; templates do the same until a layer token exists.

openQuestions: Detail heading level: h1-on-narrow / h2-on-wide, or always h2 under a (possibly visually hidden) area h1?
